claims.statement: KNF identifies registration and legal requirements for insurance agency activity in Poland.
URE reported more than 1.6 million Polish microinstallations at the end of 2025, nearly all recent growth being prosumer photovoltaics.

contrary_evidence: Existing general-liability insurers may see the niche as too small for a dedicated product.
Manufacturer warranties may absorb many losses before insurance is relevant.

economics.acquisition_route: Unvalidated hypothesis: distribute through renewable wholesalers and the parents' contractor network.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Unvalidated hypothesis: 4,000 insured contractors with proprietary loss data could support a 5 million PLN founder net-worth path in eight to twelve years.
economics.founder_time: Unvalidated hypothesis: insurer operations and outsourced claims handling keep founder work below 20 hours weekly during pilot.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Unvalidated hypothesis: data-led distribution could reach 60% gross margin, and every commercial number including capital_required_pln is hypothetical.
economics.payback: Unvalidated hypothesis: acquisition pays back within one annual policy cycle.
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: earn 12% policy commission plus 150 PLN per administered claim.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Unvalidated hypothesis: annual renewals and expanding insured installation fleets create repeat revenue.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Serial-level installation and loss records improve selection, pricing, and claims triage
fingerprint.customer: Small photovoltaic, storage, and heat-pump contractors
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Equipment wholesalers and installer workflow integrations
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Embedded specialist cover, evidence capture, and claims administration through a licensed partner
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The insurer pays commission when a policy binds and pays administration fees when claims are processed
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A contractor renews cover or needs project-specific protection without credible risk differentiation

founder_fit: The family business can inform fields and failure modes without guaranteeing commercial adoption.
Quantitative underwriting fits the founder, but regulated partnership work adds social load.
risks: Insurance conduct rules and insurer approval can lengthen launch time.
Adverse selection could overwhelm an immature loss model.

structure.commercial_archetype: Licensed insurance intermediary and delegated claims-data program
structure.control_point: Policy quote, bind, and claim-administration flow embedded in installer software
structure.critical_dependency: A licensed insurer willing to delegate distribution and use the loss model

thesis: Build a registered insurance-distribution program whose underwriting edge comes from installation and claims records for small renewable contractors.
title: Renewable Installer Loss Ledger and Embedded Cover
uncertainties: No insurer commitment or credible loss-ratio dataset has been verified.
All commercial numbers including capital_required_pln are unvalidated hypotheses.
